text: Anyone else seeing a bump in online banking lockouts today? I've had three members at the window since 11:30 saying the app keeps rejecting their MFA code.
Yep, I've had two calls on the phone queue. Both got the 'verification failed' loop after a password reset. Looks like MemberSSO to me, not the core.
Same here. One member could still see balances on the card side, so CoreBanking is fine. It's just the login/MFA step.
Heads up, I'm on with ⟨NAME_0074⟩ right now. Locked out after 3 failed MFA attempts. I verified identity on the call, but should I unlock in the admin console or wait for IT?

Go ahead and unlock after full verification, Joanna. Don't reset the MFA device though, that needs IT until we know what's going on. Log it in MemberCRM with the word 'lockout' so we can pull a count.
⟨NAME_0002⟩ just called, same issue. Unlocked fine but the SMS code never arrived. Contact on file is current, I confirmed it on the call. Could be a delivery delay on the text side.
That matches mine, Zach. Codes were arriving 5+ minutes late or not at all. I'll tell members to use the authenticator app option if they have it set up.
I'm raising this with Andre in #it now. Please keep tallying lockout calls and walk-ins in the thread so I can give him a number. Don't promise members a fix time yet.
Count at the teller line is 5 so far. Two of them I walked through the unlock with Joanna's steps and they got in on the second try.

I'm at 4 on the advocate side. For anyone still locked out, I'm telling them to try again in 15 minutes and call back if the code still doesn't come. I'll email the details through once IT confirms the cause.

Quick question on drawer limits. I've got ⟨NAME_0034⟩ at my window asking for a $9,500 cash withdrawal from checking and my drawer is only holding about $7,200 after the morning rush. Do I need to go to the vault or is there a different process?
Don't short the member. Ask them to give you a few minutes, then get a vault order in. Anything over your drawer max needs a second person to verify the count anyway.
Ok, makes sense. Is the max still $10k per teller or did that change? Pretty sure the policy got updated before the holiday.

Reminder for everyone on the floor: teller drawer limit is $7,500 effective this week, down from $10k. Anything above that goes to the vault by end of day, and ask for a dual-control count on large pulls. It's in the updated cash handling procedure.
Got it, thanks Rita. So with 3 days of holiday weekend traffic, should I plan to request extra cash proactively before the afternoon?

Yes, send the request to me by 1:00 and I'll have the vault prep it. Also, Maxwell, if the withdrawal is $10k or more, remember the CTR is triggered, so make sure the ID check is documented in the system.

Side note: ⟨NAME_0009⟩ called asking about the new limits on debit card ATM withdrawals tied to ⟨ACCT_0017⟩. I'll point them to the branch for anything large. Anyone know the daily ATM cap off the top of your head?
ATM cap hasn't changed, it's still $500 per day for standard debit. Anything higher they can do in branch with ID, and we'll just plan the cash for them.
Heads up all: the core vendor posted their maintenance window for this Saturday, 11pm to 4am ET. CoreBanking will be fully down for part of it. Expect OnlineBanking and CardProcessor to be affected.
Thanks Andre. For CardProcessor, is it stand-in processing during the outage or are we hard-declining? I need to tell the branches and the card vendor which way it goes.
Vendor notice says stand-in on with the usual limits, but CardProcessor depends on CoreBanking so balances won't refresh until it's back. I'll get written confirmation from them today.

For OnlineBanking I can put up the maintenance banner Friday afternoon and flip the app to read-only messaging at 10:45pm Saturday. MemberSSO should stay up since it doesn't depend on core, so logins work but nothing will load.
Question on my side: the nightly extracts I pull from core for reporting will fail Saturday. Anyone know whether ShareRecon runs during the window? I don't want it kicking off against a half-up core.

Good catch Amy. ShareRecon is cron-scheduled for 1:30am and it'll absolutely run against whatever core gives it. I'll disable the job Saturday evening and re-enable it manually after the vendor gives the all-clear.
Hector, can you write down the disable and re-enable steps somewhere other than your head? You're the only one who really knows those scripts and I don't love that for a maintenance weekend.
Fair. I'll put a short runbook in the wiki by Thursday: how to pause the job, how to check the GL totals after, and what a bad run looks like. Honestly overdue.
I'll review it once it's up and try the steps cold, so we know someone besides Hector can follow it. Might also help me document what the output tables look like.
Ops side: ACHHub also hangs off core, so I'll tell Timothy and Larry to push the Saturday night file windows. Any ACH files that land in the window will queue and post after.
Right, and BSAWatch is downstream of core and ACHHub too, so Compliance will see a gap in monitoring. I'll give Wesley's team a heads up so they can note it.
Draft banner copy is ready. Something like: scheduled maintenance Saturday 11pm to 4am, balances and transfers unavailable. Andre, can you eyeball it before I queue it?
Looks good. Add that debit cards will still work with limits, then ship it Friday at 3pm.
Also plan: I'll be online from 10:30pm Saturday through the post-maintenance checks and will do a ShareRecon dry run Sunday morning before turning the schedule back on.
Perfect, thanks Hector. I'll check in Sunday around 7am to confirm cards and ACH are posting normally.
Heads up all: we've got two new hires starting Monday. One joins Lending as a loan processor, the other is a new teller at the main branch. Michelle is sending the full welcome email later today.
Heads up all: MemberSSO MFA rollout for members is targeted for the week of July 20. Want to pin down what could bite us before we announce anything. Anyone see conflicts?
From Ops side I'm mostly worried about the nightly stuff. If MFA enrollment spikes load on CoreBanking, does that touch the ShareRecon window?
Nice, we've needed another teller on Saturdays. Who's going to be training them? I can take some shifts if Paul wants.

Good question. ShareRecon pulls from CoreBanking starting around 11pm. MFA enrollment itself lives in MemberSSO, so no direct dependency, but the extra OnlineBanking logins could slow CoreBanking a bit at peak.
I think Paul is pairing them with you for the first week, Joseph. Check with him before you leave today so you're not surprised Monday.
Separate question: are we sending enrollment events to the warehouse? I'd like to build a dashboard for adoption % by day if so.
Will do, thanks. I'll make sure the drawer is set up and the cash handling checklist is ready.
Yes, MemberSSO can export enrollment status daily. Amy, you and Hector sync on the feed format. Aggregate counts only, nothing member-identifying.
Perfect, aggregates are all I need. Will draft a schema Monday.
Hector, honest question: if ShareRecon breaks that week, who else can fix it? Feels like it's all in your head right now.

IT side: laptops are imaged and badges are queued. I still need to confirm MemberSSO and CoreBanking access requests are approved for both. Can managers make sure the access forms are signed off by 4pm?
Fair, and yeah, it's mostly me. Those scripts are a decade of patches with almost no docs. I'll be out July 23-24 too, which is right in the rollout window.
Hector, is the loan processor getting LoanDesk and CreditPull access on day one? Kara said she wanted them shadowing files right away.
That's a risk I don't love. Hector, can you do a walkthrough doc plus a recorded session before the 17th? Amy can shadow so there's a second person.
Happy to shadow. I know the GL tables well, just not the script logic.
LoanDesk yes, it's on the ticket. CreditPull needs Kara's approval plus the permissible purpose training sign-off, so that one may slip to Tuesday if the paperwork isn't in.
Works. I'll write up the run order, the restart steps, and the known failure modes. Probably a couple hours Tuesday and Wednesday.
Got it. I'll ping Kara now and get the training module assigned so it's not the bottleneck.
Please include what Ops should check in the morning if recon fails. Right now we just ping you and wait.
Will do, a one-page checklist for Ops with the log location and when to escalate.
Also proposing a soft launch: staff and a small member pilot July 15-17, then full rollout the 20th if clean. Thoughts?
Also, let's do a quick team lunch Tuesday to welcome them. I'll grab a headcount in the thread if people are in.
+1. A pilot lets us see recon results after real MFA traffic before everyone's on it.
Agree. I'll watch the first two nightly ShareRecon runs during the pilot and report back in this channel.
I'm in for Tuesday. Please count me for the sandwich platter.
In as well. I'll drop their login sheets off at their desks before lunch so they can get set up.
Heads up: the vendor pushed the July OS patch bundle for the app servers. I'd like to get CreditPull's integration host patched this week. Hector, can you take it?
Yep. CreditPull host is easy, no scheduled jobs on it. I can do it Wednesday after 6pm. The one I'm nervous about is the ShareRecon box.
Why that one specifically? It's on the same patch baseline.

The scripts lean on an older Python runtime and a couple of cron wrappers I wrote years ago. The bundle bumps the Python minor version, so the nightly share/GL recon could break silently. I'd want to test in a clone first.

Ops perspective: if ShareRecon fails overnight we don't find out until the GL variance report the next morning, and that delays settlement sign-off. Can we avoid patching it on a Thursday or month-end?
Is any of that documented? I've read the repo, but the wrapper logic isn't in the README. Honestly Hector is the only one who could debug it at 2am, which worries me.
Fair point. Not documented enough. I'll write a runbook while I test the clone. Amy, if you can shadow me on the dry run, that'd spread the knowledge around a bit.

Plan then: CreditPull gets patched Wednesday evening. ShareRecon gets cloned and tested first, and we hold the prod patch until the runbook exists and Amy has done the dry run. Target is the week of the 20th, not month-end.
Works for me. Please post the planned window in here once it's set so I can warn the settlements folks.
Happy to shadow. I'll block Thursday afternoon for the clone test.
Quick one: a member just asked to withdraw $9,500 cash from checking. Our drawer limit is $5,000 per teller before we need vault approval, right? Don't want to get this wrong.
Yep, $5,000 at the window without a supervisor override. Anything above that needs the vault cash order form and a manager sign-off. Also give the member a heads-up that it may take a few minutes.
And anything over $10,000 triggers the CTR, so $9,500 is under, but be careful if they've already taken cash out today. Check the day's aggregate in CoreBanking before you hand it over.
Good call, Nichole. Looked at the aggregate and there was nothing earlier today on ⟨ACCT_0099⟩. Member says it's for a car purchase from a private seller.
Fair. Just do the usual conversation about why they're carrying that much cash and note it in MemberCRM. A cashier's check might be safer for them anyway. Offer it if they're open to it.
Offered. They're fine with a cashier's check for most of it and $1,500 cash. Thanks both, that saves a trip to the vault.
Heads up for the floor: my drawer was over the $15,000 max after the morning deposits. I'm doing a cash-out to the vault at 1:45 if anyone needs me to hold off on large withdrawals until then.
Thanks Jonathan. Remember the buy-back needs two people for the count and both initials on the slip. Auditors flagged a missing initial last quarter.
Got it. Catherine, can you be my second count at 1:45?
Sure, I'll be there. Just finishing with ⟨NAME_0044⟩ first.
Anyone seeing card declines this afternoon? I've got ⟨NAME_0009⟩ on hold, says the debit card got declined at a gas pump twice. Checking account a_00017 shows plenty available.
⟨NAME_0009⟩ is one of mine. Did you check whether the card got flagged for fraud or if there's a travel/usage block on it? Pay-at-pump often triggers a $1 or $100 preauth hold.
No block showing on the card profile. Preauth could be it though, I'll look at the pending auth list for ⟨ACCT_0017⟩.
FWIW I just ran a card purchase for a walk-in and the auth went through fine, so I don't think it's a processor-wide thing. Probably just this card.

Found it. Two pending preauths from the pump, $100 each, which took available balance under the amount of the third attempt. Both should drop off, but the member needs to wait. Also confirmed the card ending in ⟨CARD_0006⟩ is active with no flags.

Good catch, Nichole. Tell the member holds usually release within 1-3 business days depending on the merchant. If it's urgent, you can transfer from savings to cover it. Please note it in MemberCRM so we have a trail.
We might want a quick member tip sheet on pay-at-pump holds. That's the third call this month I've heard about. I can draft one if Paul is okay with it.
Yes please, Catherine. Send me a draft by Friday and I'll run it past Zachary and the other advocates before we post it.

Reminder: ⟨NAME_0036⟩ called asking if we can raise their daily cash withdrawal limit for next week. I told them limits are set by Compliance and Paul, so I'll send the request there. Please don't promise anything at the window.
Agreed. ⟨NAME_0036⟩ is in my book, so loop me in and I'll follow up with them once Paul and Wesley respond.
Morning all. Quick question on disputes: ⟨NAME_0044⟩ just called about a debit card charge they don't recognize on checking. Do I file the dispute myself or hand it to an Advocate?
You can start it, Jonathan. Confirm the card is still active, and if they don't recognize it, block and reissue first. Then open the dispute form in CoreBanking with the transaction date and amount.
Got it. Card ending is on file as ⟨CARD_0026⟩, so I'll block that now. Do I need a signed affidavit before the provisional credit?

Affidavit is required for unauthorized claims, yes. Email it through secure message, not regular email. The 10 business day clock for provisional credit starts when you log the claim, so log it today.
Perfect, thanks Catherine. Logging it now.
Reminder for the floor: when you write dispute notes in MemberCRM, don't paste full card or account numbers. Use last four only or the placeholder reference. Audit flagged a couple last month.
Oops, guilty. I'll clean up my notes on ⟨ACCT_0098⟩ this morning. Is there a way to edit them or do I need to ask someone?
You can edit your own notes within 30 days. After that, send me the link and I'll redact it.
Ops heads up: the CardProcessor chargeback batch goes out at 3 PM today. Any disputes that need to be in this cycle must be fully logged with documentation by 2:30.
Thanks Rita. Does that include the one Jonathan just opened? The affidavit won't be back by then probably.
No, it can slip to tomorrow's batch. We only need the claim logged for the provisional credit timing. Chargeback submission can wait for the signed form.
Another one: ⟨NAME_0086⟩ is asking about a transfer out of their savings that they say they didn't authorize. That's not a card dispute, right? Who owns that?
Right, that's an ACH or transfer claim, different process. Don't promise any credit. Loop in the Advocate, Zachary is their RM, and flag it to Compliance since the account is high risk.
Understood. I'll note the call on ⟨ACCT_0176⟩ and pass it to Zachary and Compliance now. Appreciate it.
Heads up, saw the notice that starting August 3 branch lobby hours shift to 9:00-5:00 Mon-Thu, and Friday stays 9:00-6:00. Drive-thru unchanged. Anyone know if the Saturday morning hours are staying?
Saturday is staying 9-12 as far as I read. The only change is the weekday lobby close moving up an hour from 6:00.
Does this affect the cash-in-transit pickup schedule at all? Asking because we sometimes line up large currency reviews around the afternoon deposits.
Good question. I think the armored carrier pickup is a separate contract, so no change, but I'll confirm with Rita Solano in Operations and post back here.
Website and mobile app both show branch hours. I'll check with Andre whether those come from a config file or a content page so we can update them before August 3. Will open a ticket.
Please also check the loan application confirmation emails. I think the template says 'visit us until 6 PM' for document drop-off.
Good catch Richard, I'll add that template to the ticket. Probably a few other places with hardcoded hours too, like the IVR greeting.
Quick reminder for anyone who does member-facing work: the new hours apply to lobby only, so Member Services will still be on phones until 6:00. Don't tell people we're fully closed at 5.
Thanks Chris. Is that written down anywhere? I'd like to link it in the data dictionary note for our call-volume dashboards, since the staffing windows change.
Update: Rita confirmed the armored carrier schedule is unchanged. Pickups stay at 3:30 daily, so nothing to adjust on our side.
Morning all. Already had three members call in locked out of online banking since 7:45. All getting the "verify your identity" loop on MFA. Anyone else seeing this?
Yep, two here. One said the text code never arrives. I'm guessing this is MemberSSO since OnlineBanking relies on it for MFA. Core looks fine, I can pull up shares without issue.
Teller line has a member at my window who can't log in on mobile. Wants to move money between savings and checking. I can do it in branch, but should I also tell him to wait on resetting anything?
Joseph, yes please hold off on resets for now. Repeated resets can trigger more lockouts. Do the transfer at the window and note it in MemberCRM. I'm pinging IT in #it now.
Got ⟨NAME_0051⟩ on the phone, same issue. Verified by hand using the callback on file, and they're fine to wait. Logging it so we can count the tickets for IT.
Update: ⟨NAME_0001⟩ called back, said the code finally arrived at ⟨PHONE_0001⟩ but about 12 minutes late. So looks like delay rather than outright failure.
Thanks, that matches what Hector is seeing. SMS provider queue backed up on the MFA side. He says it's clearing. Keep tallying calls with a lockout tag and I'll send the count to IT by noon.
Will do. Count so far on my side is 6. I'll tell members to wait 5 minutes between code requests instead of hammering resend.
Morning. Two structuring alerts came out of the overnight BSAWatch run. One on ⟨NAME_0042⟩: three cash deposits in four days, each just under $10k aggregate-wise. Pulling the CTR history now.

Heads up, I'm working the CTR queue for the week. Two cash deposits crossed the $10k line today and both are in draft. One is the commercial operating account for ⟨NAME_0059⟩, the other is a member share savings deposit.

Thanks Monica. Reminder we have 15 calendar days from the transaction date to file with FinCEN, so no real pressure, but let's not let drafts sit. Did you check for aggregation across the business day?
Yes. For ⟨NAME_0059⟩ I rolled up the branch deposit plus the ATM envelope deposit into ⟨ACCT_0132⟩ and it totals $14,200 in cash in. Aggregated it as a single CTR.

Question on the member one: ⟨NAME_0028⟩ made a $9,800 deposit Tuesday and a $3,500 one today into ⟨ACCT_0061⟩. Separate business days, so no CTR trigger, but I'm wondering if we should eyeball it for structuring.
Good catch. Pull the 30-day cash history and check against the member's stated income and prior pattern. If it looks consistent, document it and close. If not, open a case for a SAR look.
Done. The member has deposited similar cash amounts monthly since January, mostly from a seasonal side business per the CRM note. Low risk, no structuring indicators. Documenting and closing.
Quick check from me, are we on track with CTR timeliness this quarter? The board risk committee will ask next week.
Yes Gloria, every CTR this quarter has been filed within 5 days on average, zero late filings. Monica will send me a one-page summary tomorrow morning that I'll forward to you.

Morning all. Updated rate sheet is going live today at noon. Auto new/used terms dropped 25 bps across the 60 and 72 month tiers, and we're adding a 0.25% relationship discount for members with direct deposit. PDF is pinned.
Thanks Kara. Does the direct deposit discount stack with the autopay discount or is it one or the other?
They stack, but the total discount is capped at 0.50%. It's on page 2, footnote 3.
Quick one: I have a pending refinance for ⟨NAME_0026⟩ that's already in underwriting. Does the new pricing apply, or is it locked at the old rate?
If no rate lock has been issued, it reprices to the new sheet. I'd check LoanDesk for a lock date on ⟨ACCT_0057⟩ before you promise anything.
Checked. No lock on file. So the member gets the better rate, I'll call them this afternoon with the update.
Heads up from the credit side: the tier 3 floor on the sheet moved from 660 to 650 for used auto, but the matrix in our underwriting worksheet still shows 660. Which one governs?
Good catch, the sheet governs. Rita, can you update the worksheet matrix before noon so nobody gets a wrong decline recommendation?
On it. I'll push the revised matrix to the shared drive by 11:30 and ping the channel.
Also, are we still showing the old APRs on the website calculator? Marketing usually lags on this.
IT has the web update queued for noon too, same push. I'll confirm once it's live and test the calculator myself.
Matrix updated and saved to the shared drive, file name has today's date. Tier 3 floor now reads 650 for used auto.
Reached ⟨NAME_0026⟩, who was thrilled about the lower rate. I'll send the revised disclosure to ⟨EMAIL_0026⟩ for e-sign once the sheet is live.
Does ⟨NAME_0015⟩ qualify for the direct deposit discount? Their checking ⟨ACCT_0030⟩ has payroll coming in, I believe.
⟨NAME_0015⟩ is in my book. Payroll deposits have hit the last three cycles, so yes, they qualify. I'll apply the discount on the next pricing run.
Rate sheet and web calculator are both live. Calculator matches the PDF at all the tiers I tested. Shout if you see anything off.
Heads up team: two dealers called me this morning about slow decisions on auto apps. One said they waited almost 4 hours on a prime-tier deal yesterday. Anyone seeing the same thing in the queue?

Yes, partly. LoanDesk was dragging on credit pulls Tuesday afternoon, CreditPull kept timing out and we had to re-run a bunch. Things look normal today, but the backlog from Tuesday pushed some into Wednesday.

Related: ⟨NAME_0008⟩ bought through one of those dealers and they're complaining the dealer told them funding would be same day. The loan on ⟨ACCT_0015⟩ didn't book until Wednesday. Dealer is blaming us.
I can pull timestamps on the CreditPull retries if that helps. I'd rather show dealers actual turnaround numbers than just say 'we had an outage.'
Yes please, Richard. Break it out by dealer for the last 2 weeks, median time from submission to decision. I want to know if it's systemic or just Tuesday.
Fwiw one of my dealers also griped that stips requests come in piecemeal. They get 3 separate emails asking for docs instead of one list. That's on us, not the system.
Fair. I'll start sending one consolidated stip list per app. Kathleen, send me the dealer names that complained so I can prioritize their files this week.
I'll call ⟨NAME_0008⟩ back this afternoon and explain the booking timeline, and I'll loop in the dealer rep so everyone has the same story. Will post the outcome here.
Hey IT, the check printer at the Cary branch is jamming again. Third time this week. Tellers are hand-feeding paper to get cashier's checks out. Can someone look at it before the weekend?
Ugh, that's the older LaserJet right? We have a replacement fuser kit in the supply closet. Hector, can you swing by Monday, or is it urgent enough for today?
I can't get out there today, I'm heads down on the ShareRecon nightly run. It threw a weird GL mismatch warning last night and I want to babysit it. Monday morning works for the fuser.
Monday is fine as long as they can limp through the weekend. I'll tell the branch to use the lobby printer for anything non-check. Thanks Hector.
Unrelated hardware thing: two of the new card readers at the teller stations aren't showing up after the firmware push. Anyone else seeing that? Wondering if it affects the CardProcessor test feed.
Not that I've seen. The readers are USB-side only, so CardProcessor authorization shouldn't be touched. Shannon, which stations? Send me the asset tags and I'll check the driver version.
Teller stations 2 and 4. Rolling back the driver on 2 now to see if it fixes it. Will post results here.

Side note for Hector: since you're the only one who really knows the ShareRecon scripts, can you drop your notes on that GL mismatch warning in the wiki? I'd like to be able to at least triage if you're out.
Fair point, Amy. I'll write up a short runbook after the run finishes tonight. Not pretty, but it'll cover the common warnings and the restart steps.
Driver rollback fixed station 2. Doing station 4 now. Looks like the new firmware version is the culprit, so I'll hold off on pushing it to the other branches.
Heads up, two dealers called me this morning about slow decisions on indirect auto apps. One said they had a deal walk to another lender over the weekend. Anyone else hearing this?
Yes. One of the dealers emailed me about ⟨NAME_0032⟩'s app. They say it sat over 24 hours with no status update. Our promise is 4 business hours on complete packages.
Let's get specifics. Martin, which dealers and what were the turnaround times? I want to know if it's a queue issue or a stips issue.
Two of our top five dealers. Both said apps submitted Friday afternoon weren't touched until Monday morning. I'll pull the timestamps from LoanDesk and post them here.
For context on my side: we had CreditPull timeouts Friday around 3 PM. A bunch of apps got stuck waiting on bureau returns and I had to re-pull manually. That probably explains some of the delay.
Confirming. I counted 11 apps with a failed pull Friday afternoon. Most were re-run by 5, but several didn't get flagged back to the dealers. That's a comms gap on our end.
OK, so partly vendor, partly us not closing the loop. Richard, can you list every app that had a failed pull and never got a status note? Kathleen and Martin can then reach out to each dealer today.
On it. I'll have the list in the next 30 minutes or so.

Separate issue: the dealer also said the applicant, ⟨NAME_0032⟩, called them upset because nobody contacted them to confirm the loan was approved. I'd like to call the client directly, but I don't want to step on the dealer.
That app was approved Friday at 4:40, with conditions: proof of income and insurance binder. If the dealer never passed those to the client, that's likely the confusion.
Kathleen, call the dealer first, then the client with the dealer's OK. Use the number on file in the CRM, ⟨PHONE_0032⟩, and note the call in the record.

Timestamps are in. Average time from submit to first decision was 6.2 hours last week versus 3.1 the week before. Biggest spikes were Friday afternoon and this morning. Posting the export in the thread.
That's a real slip. Rita, can we put a second underwriter on the dealer queue through Wednesday? I'll also ask IT to alert us when CreditPull errors out instead of finding out from the dealers.
Yes, I can cover the morning queue and Richard can take afternoons. I'll also send the dealers a short note acknowledging the delay and the fix. Draft by 2 PM for your review.

Morning, ShareRecon flagged 6 GL differences overnight, mostly in share suspense and dividend payable. Larry and I can't tie them to anything we posted yesterday. Is it the scripts again @Hector Salas, or should we start digging?

Scripts, not you. The CoreBanking extract landed around 2:50 last night, so the 2:30 cron ran against the prior day's files and threw those 6 false differences. I patched the cron to start at 3:15 and wait for the file before it runs, then re-ran ShareRecon manually and it came back clean with 0 exceptions. The corrected report should be in your inbox now, and I'll log it on the ticket.

Quick question on address changes. ⟨NAME_0041⟩ just called asking to update their mailing address. They passed MFA, but do we still need anything in writing, or is the verbal OK for a low-risk member?

Verbal is fine if they pass full verification and it's a standard mailing address change. Log it in MemberCRM with the verification method you used. Send the confirmation notice to the OLD address too, that's the fraud control.
Got it. Does the notice to the old address go out automatically from CoreBanking or do I have to trigger it?
It's automatic once you save in CoreBanking, but check that the 'address change letter' box is ticked. It defaults off on the quick-edit screen. Got burned on that last month.
Ah, it was unticked. Good catch, Catherine. Fixed and re-saved.
Different one: a member walked in wanting to change address on their checking and also asked us to update the card shipping address. Is the card address separate from the member record?
Separate in CardProcessor. Member record update doesn't always flow to the plastic reissue address. Open a ticket for Ops to confirm the card file got the new one before any reissue ships.
Will do. Member has a replacement for ⟨CARD_0024⟩ pending so timing matters. I'll flag it urgent.
Heads up, teller line: someone asked to change the address for ⟨NAME_0043⟩ by email only, no call or visit. Looks like it came from ⟨EMAIL_0043⟩. I haven't touched anything.

Good call, Joseph. Don't process it. That member is flagged high risk and email alone isn't sufficient verification. Route it to Nichole, since she's their advocate, and she'll do a callback to the number on file.
Forwarding to Nichole now. Should I reply to the sender at all?
Just a generic note saying we need to verify by phone or in branch. Don't confirm anything about their accounts, including ⟨ACCT_0097⟩.

Reminder for everyone: if the member is changing phone AND address in the same session, treat it as elevated. Get a second verification factor and note it. We've seen account takeovers start that way.
Agreed. I'd add that if they changed the contact number to something like ⟨PHONE_0041⟩, make sure the callback goes to the previous number on file, not the new one.
Exactly right. I'll pin both points in the channel and update the checklist by Friday.

Hey team, I've got ⟨NAME_0070⟩ on the line, says their debit card got declined at a grocery store twice this morning. Checking account looks fine on my end, balance is healthy. Anyone seen decline issues today?
Nothing on my side so far. Can you see the decline reason code in the card auth log for ⟨CARD_0040⟩?
Pulling it now. Looks like it's coming back as a 'suspected fraud' hold, not insufficient funds. So the rule engine flagged it.
Catherine, before you do anything, make sure you've verified the member with the full MFA questions. If they pass, you can release the fraud hold from the card controls screen.
Already verified, they passed everything. They confirmed both grocery attempts were theirs and also a gas station charge yesterday.
FYI I had a member at the teller line earlier saying their card worked fine at the pump, so it doesn't look like a CardProcessor outage. Probably just individual flags.
Good to know Max, thanks. CoreBanking is up and the auth feed has been normal per #it, so I agree this is a one-off rule trigger.
Hold released. I told them to try a small purchase while we're still on the phone. Also noting it in MemberCRM so the history is there.
